title: About me
goal: Introduce yourself: your name, where you're from, where you live and what languages you speak — and ask others the same.
intro:
This unit gives you the personal pronouns and the verb 'to be' (**आहे**), which is the backbone of hundreds of everyday sentences.

You'll also learn a very Marathi way of talking about languages: instead of 'I know Marathi' you say मला मराठी येतं — literally 'Marathi comes to me'.

vocab.note: Inclusive 'we' (you and I) is आपण.
Respectful 'he' takes plural verbs: ते आले आहेत 'he has come'.
Present: आहे, आहेस, आहोत, आहात, आहेत. Negative: नाही, नाहीस, नाहीत.

grammar.title: Pronouns and the verb 'to be' (आहे)
grammar.body:
The present of असणे 'to be' changes with the person:

मी **आहे** — I am
तू **आहेस** — you are (informal)
तो / ती / ते **आहे** — he / she / it is
आम्ही / आपण **आहोत** — we are
तुम्ही **आहात** — you are (polite / plural)
ते / त्या **आहेत** — they are

The negative replaces आहे with **नाही**: मी नाही, तू नाहीस, तो नाही, आम्ही नाही, तुम्ही नाही, ते नाहीत.

In fast speech आहे is often shortened: मी बरा आहे → मी बराय (barāy), काय आहे → कायय.

examples.en: They are doctors. / He is a doctor (respectful).

grammar.title: Question words
grammar.body:
Question words go **where the answer would go** — usually just before the verb. Word order doesn't change.

**काय** what · **कोण** who · **कुठे** where · **कुठला / कोणता** which · **का** why · **कधी** when

For yes/no questions, add **का** at the end (or just raise your voice). Note that का at the end = question marker, but का before the verb = 'why'.

कुठला and कोणता agree in gender like adjectives: कुठला देश (m), कुठली भाषा (f), कुठलं शहर (n).

examples.en: Why did you come? (to a man)

dialogue.title: At a friend's party
dialogue.setting: Mark, a Canadian working in Pune, meets Anita at a friend's get-together.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: नमस्कार मार्क! मी अनिता. तुम्ही कुठले आहात?
lines.roman: namaskār mārk! mī anitā. tumhī kuṭhle āhāt?
lines.en: Hello Mark! I'm Anita. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.native: मी कॅनडाचा आहे. पण आता मी पुण्यात राहतो.
lines.roman: mī kænaḍātsā āhe. paṇ ātā mī puṇyāt rāhto.
lines.en: I'm from Canada. But now I live in Pune.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.native: थोडं थोडं येतं. मी शिकतो आहे.
lines.roman: thoḍaṃ thoḍaṃ yetaṃ. mī shikto āhe.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: I live in Pune too, in Kothrud.

culture: Ask a Marathi speaker where they're from and they may name two places: the city where they live and their **गाव** — the ancestral village or town their family comes from, even if they've never lived there. 'तुमचं गाव कोणतं?' is a friendly, common question. Notice the emphatic suffix **-च** (पुण्यातच 'right in Pune'), which you'll hear constantly.
